campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 20, 2026
campbell.summary: The agenda for Campbell's October 20, 2026, City Council meeting listed several recognitions, routine approvals, and two larger items: a request to extend deadlines for the next phases of the Pruneyard Center project and a proposed five-year equipment lease for a road-marking machine. The agenda also included the usual minutes, bills, and committee reports.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a public hearing on a request from the Pruneyard Center Association to extend the deadlines for Phases 3 and 4 (a five-story office building, parking structure expansions, and additional commercial buildings) and the related parcel map to December 31, 2031.
The agenda listed a proposed five-year, $159,327 lease with NCL Government Capital for a Thermoplastic Melter Trailer TPM-1500.
The agenda listed approval of bills and claims totaling $2,750,402.16 and adoption of the classification and salary schedules for Fiscal Years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027.

The agenda listed recognitions for Code Enforcement Officer Appreciation Week (October 11-17) and the Campbell Little League Senior All-Star Team, 2026 Northern California Senior League State Championship winners.
The agenda listed an introduction of the 2026-2027 Campbell Youth Commission, including a presentation of its initial work plan.

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 21, 2026
saratoga.summary: The agenda for the October 21, 2026, Saratoga City Council meeting listed routine business such as approving past meeting minutes and bill-payment registers, along with final approvals for two property splits. It also listed an annual update to the City Code and proposals to start work on a Climate Resilience District.
keyTopics: Council was asked to review and approve minutes from the September 30, 2026, special meeting and the October 7, 2026, meeting, and to accept the accounts payable check registers for 10/01/2026 and 10/08/2026.
Final map approval was on the agenda for splitting the property at 14860 Farwell Ave into two lots (parcel map application ULS25-0013).
Final map approval was on the agenda for splitting the property at 18510 Sobey Rd into two lots (parcel map application ULS25-0004).
A public hearing was listed on the 2026 annual City Code update, including proposed changes to rules on scheduling appeals and qualifications for City Commissioners, among other provisions.
The agenda listed resolutions to establish a Climate Resilience District Task Force and to start the process of establishing a Climate Resilience District.

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — October 13, 2026
los-altos.summary: The agenda for the Los Altos City Council's October 13, 2026, meeting listed a group of routine items such as meeting minutes, financial reports, and project completions, along with a housing guidelines item, a small electrification rebate funding request, and a review of the handbook for city commissions. The agenda also listed an update on Ada's Cafe at the Community Center and the council's tentative calendar tied to the Housing Element.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a resolution to appropriate $78,000 from the general fund to the residential electrification rebate program in the FY2026-27 budget.
The agenda listed approval of Below Market Rate (BMR) for-sale and rental housing guidelines, with a finding that the action is exempt from CEQA under Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3).

The agenda listed resolutions accepting two completed public works projects: the FY 2025-2026 on-call sanitary sewer spot repairs and CCTV inspection services, and the FY 2024-2025 Annual Streets Project built by O'Grady Paving, Inc.
The agenda listed a discussion of the Commission and Committee Handbook, with the council invited to give direction on revisions as needed.
The agenda listed receipt of the Treasurer's Report for the quarter ending September 30, 2026, and the Investment Portfolio Report for the quarter ending June 30, 2026.

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 20, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026, Los Gatos Town Council meeting listed routine business such as approving minutes from two October 6 meetings and receiving the town's August financial reports. It also listed several items authorizing the Town Manager to sign contracts and amendments, including an amendment with Foster and Foster, a three-year agreement, and a lease amendment.
keyTopics: The agenda listed approval of the minutes from the October 6, 2026, Special Meeting and the October 6, 2026, regular Town Council Meeting.
The agenda listed receipt of the August 2026 Expenditure and Revenue Reports and the Monthly Financial and Investment Report for August 2026.
The agenda listed approval and ratification of the Accounts Payable Check Registers and the Payroll Report.
The agenda listed authorizing the Town Manager to execute a first amendment with Foster and Foster.
The agenda listed authorizing the Town Manager or designee to enter into a three-year agreement, and authorizing the Town Manager to negotiate and execute an amendment to a lease.

san-jose.title: San José City Council — October 20, 2026
san-jose.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026, San José City Council meeting listed routine business such as minutes and event approvals, along with several larger items including the City Manager's annual report, a police auditor report, and planning work priorities. It also listed three land-use matters: a general plan amendment request and two appeals tied to specific properties.
keyTopics: The agenda listed the 2025-2026 City Manager's Annual Report and the 2025 Independent Police Auditor Year End Report.
Citywide Planning Work Plan Prioritization was listed for consideration.
An appeal of the in-fill exemption for a data center use at 300 Holger Way was listed for an administrative hearing.

An administrative hearing on environmental and site development permit appeals for 470 West San Carlos Street was listed, along with early consideration of a privately initiated General Plan amendment for 525 Race Street.

Items before the Council included a conditional vacation of part of Spring Street between Asbury Street and West Taylor Street, and council-sponsored events including a District 9 farewell celebration and a Taiwan Retrocession Day proclamation and flag raising.

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee — October 26, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The agenda for the October 26, 2026, Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee meeting listed routine business such as approving past meeting minutes, plus items on subcommittee assignments, a teen wellness retreat event, and upcoming volunteer opportunities. The agenda also included a team-builder activity and a period for members of the public to speak on topics not on the agenda.
keyTopics: The agenda listed approval of minutes from a previous meeting.
A team-builder activity was on the agenda.
Subcommittee assignments were listed for the committee.
The agenda included a Teen Wellness Retreat event item.
Upcoming volunteer opportunities were listed as an agenda item.

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 6, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The agenda for the Sunnyvale City Council's October 6, 2026, evening meeting listed recognitions for local youth baseball and several community awareness observances, along with routine approvals and a few larger items on water use, worker protections, and park art. Council members were also scheduled to receive updates on completed projects covering pesticide use, artificial turf, and a possible linear park.
keyTopics: An ordinance to ban the use of drinking-quality water to irrigate nonfunctional turf, to carry out state law AB 1572, listed as a public hearing and introduction
Discussion and possible action to introduce a Service Worker Retention Ordinance
Approval of public art for the Lakewood Park renovation
A contract amendment with WSP USA Inc. for environmental consulting at the SMaRT Station and Sunnyvale Landfill, raising the cap by $160,000 to $385,000 and extending it through October 17, 2028
Recognition of the 2026 Sunnyvale Little League Junior Division All-Stars, plus Indigenous Peoples' Day, Friends of the Library Week, and Sunnyvale Stands United Against Hate Week

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — October 20, 2026
cupertino.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026, Cupertino City Council meeting listed proclamations for Domestic Violence Awareness Month, National First Responders Day, and United Against Hate Week. It also listed a consent calendar of routine items including a bridge design contract, a gymnastics program contract, and an update to the City Manager's employment agreement, plus two public hearings and a discussion of leasing a city-owned commercial property. A separate special meeting and study session was noticed for 5:45 p.m. before the 6:45 p.m. regular meeting.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a proposed $1,278,700 design services agreement with Biggs Cardoza Associates for the McClellan Road Bridge Project, along with acceptance of $850,000 in federal grant funds.
The agenda listed a proposed contract of up to $480,000 with Bay Aerials Gymnastics for gymnastics classes and camps, with authority to extend two more years for a five-year total of up to $800,000.
The action calendar listed a proposed approach for leasing the city-owned commercial property at 22100 Stevens Creek Boulevard.

Public hearings listed included updates to the Health and Safety chapter of the General Plan (with a new background report) and a hearing on conduit financing for The RISE Block 5 Apartments, postponed from October 6.

The consent calendar also listed a first amendment to the City Manager's employment agreement with Tina Kapoor and changes to the compensation program for appointed employees, as well as the first-year update of the FY 2025-2027 City Work Program.

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — October 20, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The agenda listed a special Santa Clara City Council meeting for October 20, 2026, at 5:30 pm, held in person at City Hall and online. Items before the Council included an update on the FIFA risk analysis disclosures investigation, two Council member requests about data centers, and a request about resident parking at apartment complexes.
keyTopics: The agenda listed an update on the FIFA Risk Analysis Disclosures Investigation.

Councilmember Hardy's written request asks staff to give the Council and public an update within 30 days on how new large electrical load uses, including data centers, get approvals and power allocations, with a possible moratorium on new stand-alone data centers (deferred from October 6).
Councilmember Hardy's separate request proposes a policy that would bar the City from signing non-disclosure agreements with stand-alone data centers (deferred from October 6).

Councilmember Park's written request asks the Council to consider how apartment residents can park in or near their complexes without fear of being ticketed or towed (deferred from September 22 and October 6).

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — October 20, 2026
milpitas.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026, Milpitas City Council meeting listed routine housekeeping items along with a few items of local interest, including a proposal to rename the Cesar Chavez Community Garden and Plaza and a contract amendment for a new park design. It also listed a presentation from the Santa Clara County Mosquito and Vector Control District and the annual commission work plans.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a resolution to rename the Cesar Chavez Community Garden as "Milpitas Community Garden," rename Cesar Chavez Plaza as "Milpitas Civic Center Plaza," and name the community garden in Delano Manongs Park the "Larry Itliong Community Garden."

The agenda listed an amendment to the design services agreement with Callander Associates Landscape Architecture, Inc., for the Metro Tango Subdistrict Park Project, in an amount not to exceed $130,000.
The agenda listed a presentation from the Santa Clara County Mosquito and Vector Control District.

The agenda listed acceptance of the FY2025-26 Commission Annual Report and approval of FY2026-27 work plans for eight city commissions, including the Arts Commission, the Economic Development and Trade Commission, the Library and Education Advisory Commission, and the Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources Commission.

The agenda listed routine items: the council meeting calendar for October and November 2026, minutes from the October 6, 2026, meeting, a preview of items expected at the next regular meeting, and the list of items requested by Councilmembers.

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Architectural Review Board — October 15, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The agenda listed a public hearing before Palo Alto's Architectural Review Board on a request from AT&T to add new wireless equipment to two existing city-owned wood utility poles in the public right-of-way. The poles are near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue.
keyTopics: AT&T's request (file 26PLN-00229) to add new antennas, remote radio units, and associated equipment to two existing city-owned wood utility poles, treated as two Tier 2 wireless communication facilities
Proposed seven-foot fiberglass pole extensions on the poles, located near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue
Listed as a quasi-judicial public hearing, with the project marked exempt from environmental review under CEQA Section 15301 (Existing Facilities)
A supplemental report was added to the agenda packet for this item
